chunks: And by this chain of narrators, from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Razi, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutaibah, from al-Fadl ibn Shazan, from Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam ibn Zahir, from Ismail ibn Ayyash, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wail, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) looked at his son, Husayn (peace be upon him), and said: 'Indeed, this son of mine is a master, as the Messenger of Allah named him a master. Allah will bring forth from his loins a man with the name of your Prophet, who will resemble him in appearance and character. He will emerge at a time when people are heedless, when righteousness is dead, and when injustice is manifest. By Allah, if he did not emerge, his neck would be struck. The people of the heavens and their inhabitants will rejoice at his emergence. He will fill the earth with justice, as it was filled with injustice and oppression.' The end of the report.
ai.seo_question: Who is the man from the progeny of Imam Husayn that will fill the earth with justice?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the prophetic designation of Imam Husayn as 'Sayyid' and foretells the emergence of the Mahdi, who shares the Prophet’s name and countenance. It emphasizes the cosmic joy of the heavens at his arrival and his pivotal role in establishing global justice (*adl*) to counteract the prevailing tyranny (*zulm*), a core tenet of Shia eschatology.
